items.q3: د رحمان د بندګانو ځینې صفتونه یاد کړئ.
items.a: يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ بِالتَّوَاضُعِ، وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ قَالُوا سَلَامًا، وَيَعْبُدُونَ اللّٰهَ فِي لَيَالِيهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا، وَلَا يُسْرِفُونَ وَلَا يَبْخَلُونَ، وَلَا يُشْرِكُونَ بِاللّٰهِ، وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ.
items.e: Lesson text, pages 1–2.

items.q2: What did Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say about extravagance?
items.q3: الله عزوجل د اسراف په اړه څه ویلي دي؟
items.a: قَالَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالَى: وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذٰلِكَ قَوَامًا.
items.e: Al-Furqan 67, page 1.

items.e: Page 10.

items.e: Page 9.

items.q2: Hassan entered Islam ______.

items.a: مُبَكِّرًا

items.e: Page 9.

items.a: قَالَ سَيِّدُنَا حَسَّانُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ رَضِيَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالَى عَنْهُ الشِّعْرَ فِي الْعَصْرَيْنِ الْجَاهِلِيِّ وَالْإِسْلَامِيِّ.

items.q: متنبی ایک بڑا شاعر تھا۔

items.a: كَانَ الْمُتَنَبِّي شَاعِرًا كَبِيرًا.

items.e: Page 13.

items.q: اُذْكُرْ أَهَمَّ الْمُدُنِ لِإِقْلِيمِ السِّنْدِ.

items.a: مِنْ أَهَمِّ مُدُنِ السِّنْدِ: كَرَاتْشِي (الْعَاصِمَةُ) وَسَكَّرُ وَحَيْدَرْ آبَادُ وَلَارْكَانَةُ وَتَتْهَ.
items.e: Agent answer: the lesson names Karachi and (in captions) Sukkur; the other cities are from general knowledge.

items.a: هَبَّتْ عَلَى بِلَادِ السِّنْدِ نَفْحَةُ الْإِسْلَامِ فِي عَصْرِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، ثُمَّ انْتَشَرَ الْإِسْلَامُ فِيهَا وَسَافَرَ إِلَيْهَا الْعَرَبُ وَالْعُلَمَاءُ وَالْأُدَبَاءُ، فَتَعَلَّمَ مُسْلِمُو السِّنْدِ الْقُرْآنَ وَالسُّنَّةَ وَاللُّغَةَ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ.

items.e: Page 13.

items.a: شَوَارِعُهَا وَاسِعَةٌ.

items.a: أَزِقَّتُهَا عَرِيضَةٌ جِدًّا.

items.a: يَجْرِي نَهْرٌ أَيْضًا وَسَطَ هٰذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ.

items.q: اُذْكُرْ أَهَمَّ شَوَارِعِ الْمَدِينَةِ الْمُنَوَّرَةِ.

items.a: أَنْشَأَتِ الْحُكُومَةُ السَّعُودِيَّةُ طُرُقًا مُسْفَلَتَةً وَشَوَارِعَ مُمَهَّدَةً عَرِيضَةً، فَأَصْبَحَ الْمُرُورُ مُيَسَّرًا وَسَهْلًا.

items.e: Page 78.

items.q2: Around it are modern shops …

items.a: وَالْأَسْوَاقُ التَّقْلِيدِيَّةُ الْقَدِيمَةُ.
items.e: Page 77.

items.a: جَمِيعُ سُبُلِ الرَّاحَةِ لِلْإِقَامَةِ.
items.e: Page 78.

items.e: Page 77.

items.a: بِإِزَالَةِ جَمِيعِ الْمَبَانِي الْقَدِيمَةِ.
items.e: Page 78.

items.e: Page 83.

items.a: وَدُفِنَ فِي مَقْبَرَةِ (مَكْلِي).

items.e: Page 82.

items.q: مخدوم محمد ہاشم نے عربی میں کئی کتابیں لکھیں۔

items.a: أَلَّفَ الْمَخْدُومُ مُحَمَّدُ هَاشِمٍ كُتُبًا كَثِيرَةً بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ.

items.a: أَعْطِنِي حُقْنَةً وَحَبَّتَيْنِ وَشَرَابًا لِلسُّعَالِ.

items.e: Page 89.

items.q: اُكْتُبْ آيَةَ الْوَارِدَةِ عَنِ الْمُعَاقِ.

items.q3: د معلول په اړه آیت ولیکئ.
items.a: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَي الْاَعْمٰى حَرَجٌ وَّلَا عَلَي الْاَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَّلَا عَلَي الْمَرِيْضِ حَرَجٌ﴾ (الْفَتْح: ١٧)
items.e: Page 90.

items.q: مَنْ حَرَّضَ عَلَى دَمْجِ الْمُعَاقِ فِي الْمُجْتَمَعِ؟

items.e: Page 90.

items.e: Page 90 (his blindness from general knowledge).

items.e: Page 91.

items.e: Page 89.

items.e: Page 89.

items.e: Page 90.

items.e: Page 91.

items.e: Page 89.

items.q2: Islam takes special care of the disabled and urges …

items.e: Page 90.

items.a: عُلِّمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ الرِّفْقَ وَالْمَحَبَّةَ مَعَ الضُّعَفَاءِ وَالْمَرْضَى.

items.a: اَلنَّاسُ كُلُّهُمْ سَوَاءٌ فِي الْمُجْتَمَعِ.

items.a: إِحْدَى أَخَوَاتِي مُعَوَّقَةٌ.

items.e: Page 95.

items.q2: LAN اور WAN میں فرق بتائیں۔
items.q3: د LAN او WAN ترمنځ توپیر وکړئ.
items.a: A LAN (Local Area Network) covers a small area such as a room, building or campus; it is fast, cheap and owned by one organization. A WAN (Wide Area Network) covers a large area such as cities or countries; it is slower and costlier and uses public or leased lines. The Internet is the biggest WAN.
items.e: A LAN joins computers close together, a WAN joins networks far apart.

items.q: Differentiate between wired and wireless network.
items.q2: تار والے اور وائرلیس نیٹ ورک میں فرق بتائیں۔
items.q3: د تار لرونکې او بېسیمې شبکې ترمنځ توپیر وکړئ.
items.a: A wired network connects devices with cables (twisted pair, fiber optic): it is fast, stable and secure but the devices are fixed and cabling costs money. A wireless network uses radio waves (Wi-Fi): devices can move and it is easy to set up, but it is usually slower, can be interfered with and is easier to attack.
items.e: Cables against radio waves.

items.q: In the high rate of distortion in communication environment which of the following communication media is most appropriate?
items.q2: مواصلاتی ماحول میں بگاڑ کی بلند شرح کی صورت میں درج ذیل میں سے کون سا مواصلاتی ذریعہ سب سے موزوں ہے؟ الف۔ کوایکسیل کیبل ب۔ ٹوئسٹڈ پیئر کیبل ج۔ فائبر آپٹک کیبل د۔ ٹی وی کیبل
items.q3: په مخابراتي چاپېریال کې د لوړې ګډوډۍ په صورت کې لاندې کومه مخابراتي رسنۍ تر ټولو مناسبه ده؟ الف. کوایکسیل کیبل ب. ټوېسټډ پېر کیبل ج. فایبر اپټیک کیبل د. ټي وي کیبل
items.e: Fiber optic cable carries light signals, so electrical noise and distortion do not affect it.

items.q: The connection of computers in a small geographical area is called:
items.q2: چھوٹے جغرافیائی علاقے میں کمپیوٹرز کے باہمی رابطے کو کہتے ہیں: الف۔ LAN ب۔ MAN ج۔ WAN د۔ PAN
items.q3: په وړوکې جغرافیايي سیمه کې د کمپیوټرونو اړیکه ویل کېږي: الف. LAN ب. MAN ج. WAN د. PAN
items.e: A LAN (Local Area Network) connects computers in a small area such as a room, building or campus.

items.q: Which Technology creates computer-generated simulation?
items.q2: کون سی ٹیکنالوجی کمپیوٹر سے تیار کردہ نقل بناتی ہے؟ الف۔ کمپیوٹر کی مدد سے ترجمہ ب۔ تقسیم شدہ ایپلی کیشنز ج۔ ورچوئل ریئلیٹی د۔ مشین لرننگ
items.q3: کومه ټکنالوژي د کمپیوټر جوړ شوی نقل جوړوي؟ الف. د کمپیوټر په مرسته ژباړه ب. ویشل شوي اپلېکېشنونه ج. مجازي واقعیت د. ماشین زده کړه
items.e: Virtual Reality creates a computer-generated simulation of a 3D environment.

items.q: Which technology uses laser beams to create images?
items.q2: کون سی ٹیکنالوجی تصاویر بنانے کے لیے لیزر شعاعیں استعمال کرتی ہے؟ الف۔ مصنوعی ذہانت ب۔ تھری ڈی ہولوگرافک امیجنگ ج۔ روبوٹکس د۔ تقسیم شدہ ایپلی کیشنز
items.q3: کومه ټکنالوژي د انځورونو جوړولو لپاره د لیزر وړانګې کاروي؟ الف. مصنوعي هوښیارتیا ب. 3D هولوګرافیک انځورګري ج. روبوټیکس د. ویشل شوي اپلېکېشنونه
items.e: 3D holographic imaging uses laser beams to create three-dimensional images.

items.q: Which technology provides telecommunication at high speed?
items.q2: کون سی ٹیکنالوجی تیز رفتار ٹیلی کمیونیکیشن فراہم کرتی ہے؟ الف۔ ورچوئل ریئلیٹی ب۔ تقسیم شدہ ایپلی کیشنز ج۔ روبوٹکس د۔ 5G
items.q3: کومه ټکنالوژي چټکه مخابره برابروي؟ الف. مجازي واقعیت ب. ویشل شوي اپلېکېشنونه ج. روبوټیکس د. 5G
items.e: 5G is the fifth generation of mobile technology, giving very high-speed telecommunication.

items.q: What are the benefits of using networks?
items.q2: نیٹ ورکس استعمال کرنے کے کیا فوائد ہیں؟
items.q3: د شبکو د کارولو ګټې کومې دي؟
items.a: Networks let users share resources (printers, files, the Internet connection), send messages and data quickly, keep data in one place with central backup and security, save money on hardware and software, and work together on the same task.
items.e: These are the main benefits of connecting computers.

items.q: What is the role of network switch?
items.q2: نیٹ ورک سوئچ کا کیا کردار ہے؟
items.q3: د شبکې سویچ رول څه دی؟
items.a: A switch connects the computers of a LAN. It learns the MAC address of every device and sends each message only to the computer it is meant for, while a hub sends it to all computers. This makes the network faster and reduces traffic.
items.e: The switch directs data to its destination.

items.q: List different tasks that can be performed by robots.
items.q2: ان مختلف کاموں کی فہرست بنائیں جو روبوٹس انجام دے سکتے ہیں۔
items.q3: هغه بېلابېل کارونه لیست کړئ چې روبوټونه یې ترسره کولای شي.
items.a: Robots can assemble, weld and paint cars in factories, pack and carry goods, clean homes, work in laboratories, help in surgery, explore space and the sea, defuse bombs and do dangerous or repeated jobs.
items.e: Robotics is used in automobile manufacturing, packaging, laboratory research and cleaning homes.

items.q: Why distributed applications are used?
items.q2: تقسیم شدہ ایپلی کیشنز کیوں استعمال کی جاتی ہیں؟
items.q3: ویشل شوي اپلېکېشنونه ولې کارول کېږي؟
items.a: A distributed application runs on several computers in a network at the same time. It is used when the workload is too much for a single server, so the work is shared; it also keeps working if one computer fails and serves users in different places. Examples: cellular networks, social networks, online banking, supermarket check-out systems.
items.e: The book: used when the workload is too much for a single server.

items.q: What is the purpose of blockchain technology?
items.q2: بلاک چین ٹیکنالوجی کا مقصد کیا ہے؟
items.q3: د بلاک چین ټکنالوژۍ موخه څه ده؟
items.a: Blockchain records digital information (for example bank transactions) in blocks that are closed and linked into a chain; the information cannot be changed or deleted, so the record is secure and can be shared safely without a middleman.
items.e: The purpose is secure recording and sharing of digital information.

items.q: Describe 3D holographic imaging.
items.q2: تھری ڈی ہولوگرافک امیجنگ بیان کریں۔
items.q3: 3D هولوګرافیک انځورګري تشریح کړئ.
items.a: 3D holographic imaging uses laser beams to create three-dimensional images called holograms. A hologram shows objects and animations that seem real; it exists freely in space and a person can walk around it and see it from all sides.
items.e: Definition from the book.

items.q: Write down the uses of Microsoft Excel.
items.q2: مائیکروسافٹ ایکسل کے استعمالات لکھیں۔
items.q3: د مایکروسافټ ایکسل کارونې ولیکئ.
items.a: Excel is used to enter and store data in rows and columns, do calculations with formulas and functions, sort and filter data, draw charts and graphs, and prepare budgets, marks sheets, accounts and other reports.
items.e: Excel is a spreadsheet program.

items.a: The formula bar shows the contents (data or formula) of the active cell and is used to enter or edit them.

items.q2: ورک شیٹ اور ورک بک میں فرق بتائیں۔
items.q3: د ورک شیټ او ورک بوک ترمنځ توپیر وکړئ.
items.a: A worksheet is a single sheet, a grid of rows and columns, in which data is entered. A workbook is an Excel file that holds one or more worksheets.
items.e: One workbook contains many worksheets.

items.q: What are the steps to create a Pie chart?

items.a: 1. Enter the categories and their values in cells. 2. Select the data. 3. Click the Insert tab and, in the Charts group, choose Pie and the pie type. 4. The chart appears on the sheet. 5. Add or edit the chart title and data labels from Chart Design / Chart Elements.
items.e: A pie chart shows each value as a slice of the whole.

Write each name in the box its arrow points to.
items.e: The eleven boxes are filled with these eleven parts.

items.q: Explain the features of information processing model.
items.q2: معلومات کی پروسیسنگ کے ماڈل کی خصوصیات بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د معلوماتو د پروسس ماډل ځانګړتیاوې تشریح کړئ.
items.a: The computer's information processing model has three steps: some kind of input is obtained (data entered by the user or a device), the input is processed according to the given instructions (the program), and output is generated (the result is shown or stored).
items.e: Input, then processing, then output.

items.e: Steps from section 3.2.1.

items.q: How nested loops are useful in arranging a calendar?
items.q2: کیلنڈر ترتیب دینے میں نیسٹڈ لوپس کیسے مفید ہیں؟
items.q3: په کیلنډر ترتیبولو کې نیسټ شوي لوپونه څنګه ګټور دي؟
items.a: A calendar has weeks (rows) and days (columns). An outer loop repeats once for every week and an inner loop runs through the seven days of that week, printing the dates one after another, so a few lines of code arrange the whole month. Nested loops are useful when a repeated task has to be done many times inside another repetition.
items.e: Outer loop: weeks; inner loop: days.

items.q3: د ستونزې د پراخوالي او محدودیتونو ترمنځ توپیر وکړئ.
items.a: The scope defines the boundaries of what a solution must provide to meet the requirements; the limitations are the aspects that are beyond the study or implementation of the problem. For a calculator, the four operations (add, subtract, multiply, divide) are its scope and other operations are its limitations.
items.e: Example 1 of section 3.1.4.

items.q3: د کال لپاره ۴ عددي شمېره ان پټ واخلئ او وګورئ چې کال لیپ کال دی که نه. خپل آوټ پټ داسې وښایاست: "The year 1979 is not a leap year" یا "The year 2020 is a leap year."
items.a: A program that reads the year and checks the leap-year rule (divisible by 4 and not by 100, or divisible by 400).
items.e: year = int(input("Enter a year: ")) if (year % 4 == 0 and year % 100 != 0) or (year % 400 == 0): ​ print("The year", year, "is a leap year") else: ​ print("The year", year, "is not a leap year") 2020 gives "The year 2020 is a leap year" and 1979 gives "The year 1979 is not a leap year".

items.a: A program that reads the length and width and compares them.
items.e: length = float(input("Enter the length: ")) width = float(input("Enter the width: ")) if length == width: ​ print("It is a square") else: ​ print("It is a rectangle") A quadrilateral with all sides equal is a square; if length and width differ it is a rectangle.

items.q: The volunteers who help in prevention of cybercrime are called:

items.q3: هغه رضاکاران چې د سایبري جرم په مخنیوي کې مرسته کوي ویل کېږي:
items.e: Cyber Scouts are volunteers who help prevent cybercrime.

items.q: Who is cyber scout? How can he/she assist in prevention of cyber crime?
items.q2: سائبر اسکاؤٹ کون ہے؟ وہ سائبر کرائم کی روک تھام میں کیسے مدد کر سکتا/سکتی ہے؟
items.q3: سایبر سکاوټ څوک دی؟ هغه د سایبري جرم په مخنیوي کې څنګه مرسته کولای شي؟
items.a: A cyber scout is a person who works to spread awareness about cybercrime in society. He or she is trained to identify cybercrime activities and knows how to prevent them, so he or she can help by teaching others the risks of virtual socializing, promoting cyber safety, and reporting suspicious activity.
items.e: Section 5.8 of the book.

items.q: Why we need cybercrime laws?
items.q2: ہمیں سائبر کرائم کے قوانین کی ضرورت کیوں ہے؟
items.q3: موږ ولې د سایبري جرم قوانینو ته اړتیا لرو؟
items.a: Cybercrime laws are needed to protect users and organizations from crimes such as hacking, identity theft, online fraud and piracy, to define what is illegal and give punishments, to protect privacy and property, and to let the police (FIA) take action against criminals. Without laws, criminals could misuse computers without fear.
items.e: Laws prevent and punish cybercrime.

items.q: Why computer systems should be protected from unauthorized access?
items.q2: کمپیوٹر سسٹمز کو غیر مجاز رسائی سے کیوں محفوظ رکھنا چاہیے؟
items.q3: کمپیوټري سیستمونه ولې باید له غیرمجاز لاسرسي وساتل شي؟
items.a: Unauthorized persons (hackers) can steal or change information, get credit card or bank account details for money, damage or delete data, and invade privacy. Protecting systems with passwords, antivirus and firewalls keeps data safe.
items.e: Hackers gain unauthorized access to steal or change information.

items.q: How creator of copyright work financially benefits from it?
items.q2: کاپی رائٹ والے کام کا تخلیق کار اس سے مالی فائدہ کیسے اٹھاتا ہے؟
items.q3: د کاپي رائټ کار جوړونکی له هغه څخه مالي ګټه څنګه اخلي؟
items.a: Copyright prevents others from copying the creative work without permission, so the creator can sell or license the work and earn money from every legal copy, use or performance.
items.e: Copyright prevents copying of creative work and allows the creators to financially benefit from their work.

items.q: Why digital piracy is a crime?
items.q2: ڈیجیٹل پائریسی جرم کیوں ہے؟
items.q3: ډیجیټل پایرسي ولې جرم دی؟
items.a: Digital piracy means illegally copying digital content (music, movies, software, games, e-books) without the consent of the owner. It violates the owner's copyright, takes away the owner's income and so it is a crime.
items.e: Definition and reason from section 5.1.7.

items.q: Why hackers break into computer systems?
items.q2: ہیکرز کمپیوٹر سسٹمز میں کیوں گھستے ہیں؟
items.q3: هیکران ولې کمپیوټري سیستمونو ته ننوځي؟
items.a: Hackers gain unauthorized access to computer systems to steal or change information, or to get credit card or bank account details for financial benefit, and sometimes to damage systems.
items.e: Hacking is a cybercrime.

items.q: How spyware can be harmful?
items.q2: اسپائی ویئر کیسے نقصان دہ ہو سکتا ہے؟
items.q3: سپایویر څنګه زیانمن کېدای شي؟
items.a: Spyware spies on a computer user by gathering information about their activities. It is used to steal passwords, banking PINs and other personal information, and it gets in during installation of software from the Internet. Anti-spyware or antivirus software detects and removes it.
items.e: Spyware is a kind of malware.

items.q3: لاندې کوم د کیفیت تضمین بېلګه ده؟
items.e: Quality assurance works on the process, following the quality standards defined for the product so that defects are prevented; validation and software testing check the finished product (quality control).

items.q2: درج ذیل میں سے کون مارکیٹنگ کے عناصر ہیں؟
items.q3: لاندې کوم د بازارموندنې عناصر دي؟
items.e: The four elements (4 Ps) of marketing are product, price, promotion and place.

items.q3: د سوداګرۍ پلان بنسټیزې برخې بیان کړئ.
items.a: A business plan is a written document describing the company's goals and strategy. Its five basic components are: market need (customer needs), product design, costing, operations and marketing.
items.e: The book lists customer needs, product design, costing, operations and marketing.

items.q: Describe the four elements of marketing.
items.q2: مارکیٹنگ کے چار عناصر بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د بازارموندنې څلور عناصر بیان کړئ.
items.a: The four elements (4 Ps) of marketing are: Product (what is sold), Price (what the customer pays), Promotion (advertising and telling people about it) and Place (where and how the product reaches the customer).
items.e: Product, price, promotion and place.

items.q: What is the difference between payment and transaction?
items.q2: ادائیگی اور ٹرانزیکشن میں کیا فرق ہے؟
items.q3: د تادیې او معاملې ترمنځ توپیر څه دی؟
items.a: A transaction is an agreement between a buyer and a seller to exchange goods, services or financial assets for money; it is the act of conducting or carrying out business. A payment is the transfer of money against the purchase; it is the act of paying.
items.e: Section 6.9 and 6.10.

items.q: Why a quality assurance is important to assess the quality of a product or service?
items.q2: مصنوعہ یا خدمت کے معیار کا جائزہ لینے کے لیے کوالٹی ایشورنس کیوں اہم ہے؟
items.q3: د محصول یا خدمت د کیفیت د ارزولو لپاره د کیفیت تضمین ولې مهم دی؟
items.a: Quality assurance ensures the quality of products or services given to customers by improving the development process and making it efficient and effective according to the quality standards. It helps the company make a product that meets customers' expectations, which builds trust and loyalty.
items.e: Section 6.5.

items.q: Write down three advantages and three disadvantages of digital marketing.
items.q2: ڈیجیٹل مارکیٹنگ کے تین فوائد اور تین نقصانات لکھیں۔
items.q3: د ډیجیټل بازارموندنې درې ګټې او درې زیانونه ولیکئ.
items.a: Advantages: it removes geographical barriers; costs fall through automation and electronic media; responses are faster for marketers and users (also extremely low risk, customer loyalty, more exposure). Disadvantages: it depends fully on technology; security and privacy issues may arise; maintenance cost is high in a constantly changing environment (also price competition and worldwide competition).
items.e: From the lists in section 6.11.

items.q: Explain the term "eye level".
items.a: The horizontal line in front of our eyes is called the eye level. An object can be seen on the eye level, above the eye level or below the eye level.
items.e: Basic of perspective drawing.

items.e: Drawing without using geometrical instruments is called free hand sketching.

items.q: What is free hand sketching?
items.a: Drawing without using geometrical instruments is called free hand sketching. It needs a good deal of observation and practice; the key to good sketching is to identify the position and direction of the lines.
items.e: Done with the hand only.

items.q: ______________ paper is used to reduce or enlarge the size of an image.
items.a: Graph
items.e: Graph paper (equally spaced horizontal and vertical lines making equal squares) is used to copy an image and to enlarge or reduce its size.

items.q: What do you mean by perspective?
items.a: Perspective is a technique used by artists and designers to show three dimensional (3D) objects on a two dimensional picture plane so that they look realistic and natural. The size of objects changes with distance (near objects look larger and far-away objects smaller), which creates the illusion of depth.
items.e: Perspective gives depth to a flat drawing.

items.q: Honey comb is a good example of ______________ shape.
items.a: hexagonal (polygon)
items.e: The most beautiful hexagons in nature are the honey combs made by honeybees.

items.q: Define polygons.
items.a: A polygon is a shape bounded by more than two straight lines, for example a triangle, rectangle or square. Polygons may be regular or irregular and are seen in nature, such as the hexagonal honey comb and crystals.
items.e: Definition from the book.

items.a: three dimensional
items.e: A 3D form has length, width and depth, for example a cube, cone or cylinder.

items.q: Combination of two or more than two solids form a ______________ solid.
items.a: compound
items.e: A combination of two or more solids creates a compound solid.

items.q: How compound solids are formed?
items.a: A solid is a three dimensional form such as a cube, cone or cylinder. When two or more such solids are combined (joined, placed on or inside each other), they form a compound solid.
items.e: For example a cylinder with a cone on top.

items.q: Arrangement of art elements is called ______________.
items.a: composition
items.e: Composition is the arrangement of art elements such as line, shape, volume, colour, value and texture according to the principles of art.

items.q: In art balance means ______________ balance.
items.a: visual
items.e: Balance in art means visual balance: arranging the art elements so that the picture gives a sense of balance.

items.q: Arrangement of different objects which give the impression of oneness is called ______________.
items.a: harmony
items.e: Harmony is the combined effect of similar or related art elements that gives visual satisfaction; each landscape has its own strong harmony or oneness.

items.q: The use of complementary colours in an artwork is called ______________.
items.a: contrast
items.e: Contrast is often created by using complementary colours (such as red and green) or extremely light and dark tones.

items.q: Red, yellow and blue are ______________ colours.
items.a: primary
items.e: The three basic colours red, yellow and blue are called primary colours; all other colours are made by mixing them.

items.q: Explain composition.
items.a: Composition is the arrangement of art elements such as line, shape, volume, colour, value and texture according to the principles of art (movement, harmony, variety, balance, rhythm, emphasis and contrast). A good composition makes the artwork interesting and pleasing.
items.e: Definition from the book.

items.q: Define texture. What are the main types of texture?
items.a: Texture is the tactile quality of a surface: its smoothness or roughness (for example tree bark, rock, a wall or glass). The main types are: 1. real or tactile texture, which is felt by the sense of touch, and 2. visual texture, which is only seen and is made to look like texture with lines, tones and colours in a drawing or painting.
items.e: Types of texture.

items.q: What do you mean by the terms light, shade and shadow?
items.a: Light creates different tones and tints on an object. The area directly hit by the light glows almost white and is called the highlight; the back side of the object looks darker and is called the body shadow (shade); between them is the body tone. The shadow that an object casts on a surface or another object is called the cast shadow. Correct placing of these tones gives the illusion of volume.
items.e: From the study of the sphere in the book.

items.q: ______________ is commonly used to make models.
items.a: Clay (modelling clay)
items.e: Making objects from modelling clay is a favourite activity of many students.

items.q: In plasticine ______________ is used instead of water.
items.a: oil
items.e: Plasticine is a non-toxic oil-based clay, so it does not dry out.

items.q: For what purpose plasticine is being used.
items.a: Plasticine is a non-toxic oil-based modelling clay that does not dry out. It is used to make models and sculptures and to form realistic shapes, and mistakes can be corrected easily.
items.e: It was invented by William Harbutt in 1897.

items.q: Design is transferred with the help of ______________ two other surfaces.
items.a: printing (stencil or block printing)
items.e: In the printing techniques the motif is transferred again and again to another surface. The word 'two' in the book's sentence means 'to'.

items.q: Card board or x-ray sheet is commonly used to make ______________.
items.a: stencils
items.e: The motif is transferred to the cardboard or x-ray sheet and cut out to make the stencil.

items.q: What is stencil and for what purpose it is used.
items.a: A stencil is a sheet of cardboard or x-ray sheet in which the positive area of a motif has been cut out. Colour is applied through it to print the same motif again and again on almost any surface, including 3D and round surfaces such as vases and pots; the technique saves time.
items.e: Stencil printing.

items.q: The use of ______________ on cloth is very old.
items.a: blocks (block printing)
items.e: Using blocks for printing on clothes is a very ancient technique.

items.q: How will you make a block?
items.a: Material: a soft wooden board (3 x 3 or 4 x 4 inches), engraving tools, paper and pencil. Draw the design on paper first and transfer it to the wooden block. Carefully engrave (cut away) the negative areas of the design with the engraving tool, avoiding injury, so that the positive design stands out. Colour the raised design and press it on the cloth or sheet.
items.e: Block making.

items.q: Arrangement of objects in a still life drawing is called ______________.
items.a: composition
items.e: Arrangement of objects in a still life drawing is called composition.

items.q: Most artists always carry a ______________ with them.
items.a: sketchbook
items.e: It allows them to observe and sketch landscapes, portraits, architecture and nature.

items.q: In an artwork the area covered by the object is called ______________ space.
items.a: positive
items.e: Positive space is the area that is the object; negative space is the area around it.

items.q: Tonal contrast gives the objects a ______________ look.
items.a: three dimensional (3D)
items.e: Light and dark tones (tonal contrast) build up the form of the objects and make them look solid, three dimensional and realistic.

items.q: Why observation is necessary in drawing.
items.a: Observation is the most important element to draw an object or a landscape. We observe whether lines are vertical, horizontal, diagonal, straight or curved, and also colours, tones and tints, shades and shadows, textures, shapes and sizes. Artists make their sketches on the basis of keen observation, which also builds ideas and the sense of observation.
items.e: Observation comes before drawing.

items.q: What is positive and negative space?
items.a: Space shows the relation between different objects in a drawing. Positive space is the area in a work of art that is the object itself; negative space is the area around the object.
items.e: See the figures of the book.

items.q: What is landscape drawing?
items.a: Landscape drawing is drawing a natural view (trees, hills, sky, a path) with free hand. First make a light outline sketch (horizon line, masses of the trees, the path), then add basic tone and body shadows, then details, cast shadows and textures in the nearest objects; objects farther away are lighter and less detailed, which gives the feeling of depth and distance.
items.e: Keen observation of shapes, angles, colours and tones is needed.

items.q: Define exhibition.
items.a: The display of paintings or any kind of art works for the public in art galleries, halls or open places is called an exhibition.
items.e: It links the public and the artist.

items.q: What are the essential conditions for exhibition?
items.a: Display the works in a place with sufficient and proper light; at eye level so that the viewer is comfortable; not too close to each other, with proper space so that it does not look crowded; ask the viewers not to touch the artworks; stick a tag with the title (and the price if for sale) nearby; in a group exhibition show the works in separate groups with the artists' names; and have variety in the works and sizes to avoid monotony.
items.e: How to display.

items.q: A response to any kind of artwork is called ______________.
items.a: art communication
items.e: A response to an artwork (painting or drawing) and talking and writing about it is art communication.

items.q: ______________ remained the source of enjoyment and communication among humans throughout the history.
items.a: Images (art)
items.e: Images are the source of enjoyment, personal expression and communication among humans throughout the history.

items.q: Artist express his feelings through colours ______________ and ______________.
items.a: shapes and images
items.e: Artists express their feelings, observations and ideas through colours, shapes and images.

items.q: What is art communication?
items.a: A response to any kind of artwork (painting or drawing), and then talking and writing about it, is called art communication. It is important for art education, and for it we must learn and use the appropriate terms related to art.
items.e: Definition from the book.

items.q: ______________ is important to preserve and display an artwork.
items.a: Framing
items.e: Framing is important to preserve and display an artwork.

items.q: Artwork must be displayed in a place with sufficient and proper ______________.
items.a: light
items.e: Display in a place with sufficient and proper light.

items.q: Why it is necessary to frame the picture?
items.a: Framing is important to preserve and display an artwork: it protects the picture from damage and dust, and a frame of suitable colour improves the look and attraction of the painting.
items.e: Unframed work is kept in a portfolio.

items.q: Complete the mind map and write the summary of the lesson "The Justice of Rasoolullah (ﷺ)".
items.q2: ذہنی نقشہ مکمل کریں اور سبق "رسول اللہ ﷺ کا انصاف" کا خلاصہ لکھیں۔
items.q3: ذهني نقشه بشپړه کړئ او د لوست "د رسول الله ﷺ عدالت" لنډیز ولیکئ.
items.a: Mind map: centre - The Justice of Rasoolullah (ﷺ); branches - the land dispute, an inquiry into the claims, fair treatment of both parties, "a piece of fire" warning to the one who takes another's right. Summary (model): Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) judged a land dispute by hearing both parties and asking for evidence. He warned that whoever takes another person's right by a false claim takes a piece of fire. The lesson teaches that justice must be done for everyone, rich or poor, Muslim or not.
items.e: One possible answer based on the lesson.

items.q: After brainstorming and developing ideas, write a simple and unified paragraph of about 50 to 60 words on "Patience of Hazrat Muhammad Rasoolullah (ﷺ)" using a clear topic sentence, specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers.
items.q2: ذہنی مشق اور خیالات کی ترقی کے بعد "حضرت محمد رسول اللہ ﷺ کا صبر" پر تقریباً 50 تا 60 الفاظ کا سادہ اور مربوط پیراگراف لکھیں جس میں واضح موضوعی جملہ، مخصوص الفاظ، جاندار افعال اور تعریفی الفاظ ہوں۔
items.q3: د ذهن چمتو کولو او مفکورو وده کولو وروسته د "حضرت محمد رسول الله ﷺ صبر" په اړه شاوخوا 50 تر 60 کلمو ساده او یو شان پراګراف ولیکئ چې روښانه موضوعي جمله، ځانګړې کلمې، ژوندي فعلونه او تعریفي کلمې ولري.
items.a: Model answer (about 55 words): The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) showed great patience in every hardship. When people insulted him and threw stones at him in Taif, he calmly prayed for their guidance instead of cursing them. He listened kindly to the rude and forgave his enemies. His patient character teaches us to stay calm, forgive others and trust Allah.
items.e: Topic sentence, specific words, vivid verbs and modifiers; one possible answer.

items.q: Describe an event of justice from the life of Hazrat Muhammad Rasoolullah (ﷺ).
items.q2: حضرت محمد رسول اللہ ﷺ کی زندگی سے انصاف کا ایک واقعہ بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د حضرت محمد رسول الله ﷺ د ژوند څخه د عدالت یوه پېښه بیان کړئ.
items.a: Once two heirs disputed the ownership of a cottage built on land that belonged to two brothers. They came to the Prophet (PBUH), who sent Hazrat Huzaifa bin Yaman (RA) to the site. Hazrat Huzaifa investigated, recorded statements and took evidence from witnesses, and then gave his decision to the Prophet (PBUH), who considered it and approved it. (Another event: a Quraish woman found guilty of stealing was punished, and the Prophet refused to let Hazrat Osama (RA) plead for her, saying earlier nations were ruined because they punished the poor and forgave the rich.)
items.e: From the lesson.

items.q: What is referred to as "A piece of fire" by Hazrat Muhammad Rasoolullah (ﷺ)?
items.q2: حضرت محمد رسول اللہ ﷺ نے "آگ کا ٹکڑا" کس کو فرمایا؟
items.q3: حضرت محمد رسول الله ﷺ د "اور ټوټه" څه ته ویلي دي؟
items.a: Deceiving a judge to get a decision in one's favour (by false witnessing or unfounded evidence) is what the Prophet (PBUH) called "a piece of fire", because a wrong cannot be made right by the judge's decision.
items.e: From the lesson.

items.q: Why was an inquiry initiated by Hazrat Muhammad Rasoolullah (ﷺ) while resolving the land dispute?
items.q2: زمین کا تنازعہ حل کرتے وقت حضرت محمد رسول اللہ ﷺ نے تحقیق کیوں شروع کی؟
items.q3: د ځمکې شخړې د حل پر مهال حضرت محمد رسول الله ﷺ ولې څېړنه پیل کړه؟
items.a: Because in the justice system of the Prophet (PBUH) a judge decides according to evidence, so the facts had to be found first: the investigator went to the site, recorded the statements of people and took evidence from witnesses before the decision was made.
items.e: From the lesson.

items.q: How does the Holy Quran emphasize justice?
items.q2: قرآنِ پاک انصاف پر کیسے زور دیتا ہے؟
items.q3: قرآن کریم په عدالت څنګه ټینګار کوي؟
items.a: The Holy Quran commands believers to stand firm for justice as witnesses for Allah even against themselves, their parents or close relatives, whether the person is rich or poor (4:135), and not to let hatred of a people make them act unjustly, even with enemies, because being just is nearer to righteousness (5:8). It also tells us that the Prophet (PBUH) is an excellent example for us (33:21).
items.e: From the lesson.

items.q: What is the main idea of the lesson?
items.q2: سبق کا مرکزی خیال کیا ہے؟
items.q3: د لوست مرکزي مفکوره څه ده؟
items.a: The Prophet (PBUH) gave everyone his or her due without fear or favour, whether the person was rich or poor, friend or foe, and he showed that no one is more firm for justice than he was. His example guides people of all times.
items.e: Main idea of the lesson.

items.q: How many people are there in the poem? How do they know each other? How do you know? Can you do it?
items.q2: نظم میں کتنے لوگ ہیں؟ وہ ایک دوسرے کو کیسے جانتے ہیں؟ آپ کو کیسے معلوم ہوا؟
items.q3: په نظم کې څو کسان دي؟ هغوی یو بل څنګه پېژني؟ تاسو څنګه پوه شوئ؟
items.a: There are two people in the poem: the speaker, who is working in his field with a hoe, and a friend who calls to him from the road on a horse. They are friends: the friend slows his horse to "a meaning walk" and the speaker goes to the stone wall "for a friendly visit".
items.e: Can you do it? Yes: the poem itself shows it (a friend calls, the speaker stops work and goes to talk).
items.h: Discuss with your partner and answer the questions orally.

items.q: What is the setting (location, time of day, weather)? How do you know?
items.q2: منظر کیا ہے (جگہ، دن کا وقت، موسم)؟ آپ کو کیسے معلوم ہوا؟
items.q3: ډول ځای څه دی (ځای، د ورځې وخت، هوا)؟ تاسو څنګه پوه شوئ؟
items.a: The setting is the countryside: a hillside field with a road and a stone wall. The time is daytime (he is hoeing) and the weather is pleasant and dry, since the ground is "mellow" (soft and warm) and he can stand a hoe in it.
items.e: Clues from the poem: hills, hoe, road, stone wall, mellow ground.

items.q: What are the most important causes of deforestation?
items.q2: جنگلات کی کٹائی کی سب سے اہم وجوہات کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: د ځنګلونو د پرې کېدو تر ټولو مهم لاملونه کوم دي؟
items.a: The main causes are agriculture and cattle grazing (forests are cut to make farm land and grazing land for the growing demand for food), the demand for palm oil, lumber, soy and cattle, and humans cutting trees for their own needs; natural causes are volcanic eruptions, storms, floods, attacks of parasites and lightning.
items.e: From the lesson.

items.q: How does deforestation affect the environment?
items.q2: جنگلات کی کٹائی ماحول کو کیسے متاثر کرتی ہے؟
items.q3: د ځنګلونو پرې کول چاپېریال ته څنګه اغېز کوي؟
items.a: Trees take in carbon dioxide and give oxygen, so cutting them adds to the greenhouse effect and global warming; the soil loses its grip, so there is erosion, landslides and floods; and animals and plants lose their homes, so biodiversity falls.
items.e: From the lesson.

items.q: How can deforestation affect biodiversity?
items.q2: جنگلات کی کٹائی حیاتیاتی تنوع کو کیسے متاثر کر سکتی ہے؟
items.q3: د ځنګلونو پرې کول بیولوژیکي تنوع ته څنګه اغېز کولی شي؟
items.a: Forests are home to a great variety of species, so removing them reduces the number of species locally and can cause the extinction of species worldwide; about 50,000 species are lost every year and about 40% of the plant and animal species of Southeast Asia may disappear this century.
items.e: From the lesson.

items.q: Tourism has many forms. Describe the two main types in detail.

items.a: Tourism can be domestic or international. Domestic tourism is travelling within our own country; it is cheap and makes the new generation aware of the history and culture of their own country. International tourism is travelling to and staying in places outside the country; it needs a passport and a visa and has the greatest effect on the economy of developing nations.
items.e: From the lesson.

items.a: Tourists spend money on hotels, food, transport, guides and souvenirs, which creates jobs for millions of people and income for businesses and the government; international tourists also bring foreign money, and tourism encourages the building of roads, airports and hotels.

items.a: Ecotourism is travel that does not harm the environment or other people: for example not flying (planes burn much fuel and release carbon dioxide), not buying souvenirs made from endangered animals and plants, not damaging nature, and joining conservation projects. Many countries and organisations promote it to protect the environment and wildlife.

items.a: The Honest Woodcutter: A poor woodcutter was cutting wood by a river when his iron axe fell into the water. He sat down and cried. A river spirit rose and showed him a golden axe, but he said, "That is not mine." Then the spirit showed a silver axe and he said, "That is not mine either." At last the spirit showed his own iron axe and he said, "Yes, this is mine." The spirit was pleased with his honesty and gave him all three axes. Moral: honesty is always rewarded.

items.a: A farmer buys a well from his cunning neighbour, who then refuses to let him take water, saying "I sold you the well, not the water". items.a: At the beginning the Prince lived a pleasant life in a palace and did not know sorrow; he was happy only in the sense of pleasure. As a statue he saw the misery of the city and became sad and gave everything away. At the end he is truly happy, because his lead heart is chosen by God and he praises God in the city of gold; so he is happier at the end, because his happiness comes from doing good.

items.q3: څپې څه دي؟
items.a: Waves are series of crests and troughs formed on the surface of water by the dragging effect of winds. A wave does not carry water from one place to another; it moves energy through the water.
items.e: Waves, tides and currents are the three motions of ocean water.

items.q: How are Spring and Neap tides caused?
items.q2: بڑے اور چھوٹے مدوجزر کیسے پیدا ہوتے ہیں؟
items.q3: لوی او وړوکي جزر و مد څنګه رامنځته کېږي؟
items.a: Spring tides: when the Sun, Moon and Earth are in a straight line (full moon and new moon) their pulls add up, so high tides rise higher and low tides fall lower than normal. Neap tides: when the Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth their pulls work against each other, so high tides do not rise so high and low tides do not fall so low; they occur on the 7th and 21st day of the Moon.
items.e: Both are caused by the position of the Sun and Moon.

items.a: A strait is a narrow passage of water connecting two large water bodies (for example the straits of Gibraltar and Malacca). An isthmus is a narrow strip of land connecting two landmasses and separating two water bodies (for example the Isthmus of Panama and the Isthmus of Suez).
items.e: Strait: water between lands; isthmus: land between waters.

items.a: Pacific Ocean: the largest and deepest, about 165 million square kilometres, average depth about 4000 m, deepest part the Mariana Trench (about 10,924 m), with thousands of islands. Atlantic Ocean: the second largest, about 106 million square kilometres, between Europe and Africa in the east and the Americas in the west, average depth 3646 m, deepest point the Puerto Rico Trench (8600 m). Indian Ocean: the third largest, lying between Africa, Asia and Australia, with warm water. Southern (Antarctic) Ocean: the fourth largest, around Antarctica south of 60 degrees south latitude. Arctic Ocean: the smallest and shallowest, 14 million square kilometres, average depth 1000 m, around the North Pole, deepest point the Fram Basin (5665 m).

items.q: Explain the role of marine biodiversity in our environment.
items.q2: ہمارے ماحول میں سمندری حیاتیاتی تنوع کا کردار بیان کریں۔

items.a: Marine biodiversity is the variety of life in the oceans and seas. It keeps our planet healthy because marine plants and algae give oxygen and the ocean absorbs carbon dioxide. It gives food (fish and seafood), medicines and raw materials, jobs in fishing and tourism, and protects coasts (mangroves and coral reefs), so it strengthens the prosperity, health and well-being of people.
items.e: Section 1.7.

items.a: Oil and gas drilling (spills of crude oil and chemicals kill plankton, coral reefs, small fish and larvae); pollution (garbage and waste dumped into the sea); over-fishing (serious loss of marine biodiversity); ocean acidification (carbon dioxide absorbed by seawater makes it more acidic); also mangrove deforestation and rising sea levels. Only about 13% of the oceans remains untouched by human activities.

items.a: Extreme weather is a deviation from regular weather patterns: unexpected, unusual, severe or unseasonal weather that is beyond the range seen in the past. items.q3: د اقلیمي بدلونونو اصلي ګواښونه ولټوئ.
items.a: The main threats of climate change are rising sea levels, collapse of ecosystems, and frequent weather changes and severe weather. Climatic changes bring heavy rains or long dry periods, affect crops and vegetation, and may turn forests into deserts and deserts into grasslands.

items.a: Global warming is the gradual increase in the average temperature of the Earth, caused by the increase of greenhouse gases in the air (burning of fossil fuels, deforestation); temperatures have risen by about 1 degree Celsius in the last 100 years.

items.a: Polar ice and glaciers melt, sea levels rise and flood coasts and low-lying islands, weather patterns change with more floods, droughts, heat waves and storms, crops and wildlife are threatened and diseases may spread.

items.a: People of coastal areas depend on the sea: they work in fishing, boat building, ports, shipping and sea trade, salt making and tourism, and their food is mostly fish and seafood. Their weather is mild and humid, and they face storms, cyclones and floods.

items.q: What are the main causes of climate change?
items.q2: موسمیاتی تبدیلی کے بنیادی اسباب کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: د اقلیمي بدلون اصلي لاملونه کوم دي؟
items.a: Natural causes: volcanic eruptions, changes in the energy of the Sun, changes in ocean currents. Human causes (the main cause now): burning coal, oil and gas in industries, power stations and vehicles; cutting forests; waste and farming, which add carbon dioxide, methane and other greenhouse gases to the air so that the Earth becomes warmer.

items.q: Explain relationship between extreme weather and climate change.

items.a: Climate is the average weather of a place over many years; extreme weather is a severe deviation from it. As the climate warms because of greenhouse gases, extreme weather events become more frequent and stronger: more heat waves, heavier rain and floods, stronger hurricanes and longer droughts. So extreme weather is the visible result of climate change.

items.a: Use horns, loudspeakers and machines less and keep the volume of radio and TV low; fit silencers on vehicles and machines; keep factories and airports away from homes and schools; plant trees which absorb sound; make and follow laws against loud noise.
items.e: Remedies for noise pollution.

items.a: Environmental problems affect places differently: coastal areas and low islands face flooding from rising seas, glaciers and mountain areas lose ice, dry areas face drought and desertification, big cities suffer smog and noise, and developing countries such as Pakistan, where many people lack clean drinking water, suffer most from water pollution.
items.e: Different places, different effects.

items.a: Modes of transport are the ways of moving people and goods: road, railways, air and water. Road: flexible, door-to-door service and one of the cheapest, vital for internal trade. Railways: carry heavy goods and many passengers over long distances cheaply and safely. Air: the fastest but the most expensive, for urgent goods and long distances. items.q: Evaluate the importance of effective transportation for international trade.

items.q3: د نړیوالې سوداګرۍ لپاره د اغېزناک ترانسپورټ اهمیت ارزوئ.
items.a: Effective transport carries goods quickly, safely and cheaply between countries, links producers with world markets, makes imports and exports possible, lowers prices, supports industries and jobs, and increases a country's income. Sea ports, shipping, air cargo, roads and railways all help trade, so a country with weak transport loses trade and competitiveness.

items.q: What were the main causes of the defeat of Siraj ud Daulah in the battle of Plassey?
items.q2: جنگِ پلاسی میں سراج الدولہ کی شکست کے بنیادی اسباب کیا تھے؟
items.q3: د پلاسي په جګړه کې د سراج‌الدوله د ماتې اصلي لاملونه کوم وو؟
items.a: Siraj ud Daulah was betrayed by his own commander Mir Jafar and other nobles who had been won over by Robert Clive of the East India Company; most of his army did not fight; the Company's army was small but better trained, better armed and well led; and the Nawab was young and had many enemies at his court.
items.e: The treachery of Mir Jafar decided the battle of Plassey (1757).

items.q: Briefly describe the transfer of British power in India from the East India Company to the Crown.
items.q2: ہندوستان میں برطانوی اقتدار کی ایسٹ انڈیا کمپنی سے تاجِ برطانیہ کو منتقلی کو مختصراً بیان کریں۔
items.q3: په هند کې د برتانوي واک له ختیځې هند کمپنۍ څخه تاج ته لېږد لنډ بیان کړئ.
items.a: After the War of Independence of 1857 the British Parliament passed the Government of India Act 1858. The rule of the East India Company ended and India came directly under the British Crown. The Governor-General became the Viceroy, and a Secretary of State for India with a council in London controlled Indian affairs. Queen Victoria announced the change in her Proclamation of 1858.
items.e: From the Company to the Crown.

items.q: Outline the structure of the British administration in India.
items.q2: ہندوستان میں برطانوی انتظامیہ کے ڈھانچے کا خاکہ پیش کریں۔
items.q3: په هند کې د برتانوي ادارې جوړښت لنډیز وړاندې کړئ.
items.a: At the top was the British Parliament and the Secretary of State for India in London; in India the Viceroy (Governor-General) ruled with his Executive Council. The country was divided into provinces under governors, the provinces into divisions under commissioners and districts under a Deputy Commissioner (Collector), who was helped by officers in the tehsils. The Indian Civil Service ran the administration, and the army, police and law courts supported it.
items.e: The chain of command from London to the district.

items.q: What were the objectives of the British education policy in India?
items.q2: ہندوستان میں برطانوی تعلیمی پالیسی کے مقاصد کیا تھے؟
items.q3: په هند کې د برتانوي زده‌کړیزې پالیسۍ موخې کومې وې؟
items.a: The British wanted to produce a class of Indians who would serve as clerks and junior officers in their administration at low cost, to spread the English language and Western ideas, to make Indians loyal to British rule, and to replace the old Persian, Arabic and Sanskrit learning with English education.
items.e: Macaulay wanted people Indian in blood but English in taste, opinions and morals.

items.q: Specify the advantages of communication networks introduced by the British.
items.q2: انگریزوں کے متعارف کرائے گئے مواصلاتی نیٹ ورکس کے فوائد بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د انګرېزانو لخوا معرفي شویو مخابراتي شبکو ګټې ومنئ.
items.a: Railways, roads, the post and the telegraph made travel and the movement of goods faster, helped trade and the sale of farm products, let news and letters reach quickly, helped the government to control the country and move its army, and also brought people of different regions closer, which spread new ideas and national awareness.
items.e: Railways, telegraph, post and roads.

items.q: Describe the causes and results of the battle of Plassey.
items.q2: جنگِ پلاسی کے اسباب اور نتائج بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د پلاسي د جګړې لاملونه او پایلې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Causes: the Company misused its trade privileges and strengthened Fort William in Calcutta without permission; Siraj ud Daulah captured Calcutta in 1756; Robert Clive made a secret plan with Mir Jafar and other nobles to put Mir Jafar on the throne. Result: in the battle of 23 June 1757 Mir Jafar's troops stood aside, Siraj ud Daulah was defeated and killed, Mir Jafar became a puppet Nawab, the Company got wealth and power in Bengal, and this laid the foundation of British rule in India.
items.e: Plassey, 1757.

items.q: Identify Tipu Sultan as a symbol of resistance.
items.q2: ٹیپو سلطان کو مزاحمت کی علامت کے طور پر شناخت کریں۔
items.q3: ټیپو سلطان د مقاومت د نښې په توګه وپېژنئ.
items.a: Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore (1782 to 1799), was the most determined enemy of the British. He strengthened his army with modern weapons including rockets, tried to build a navy, made reforms in trade and administration, and fought the Mysore wars against the British. He refused to accept their rule and died fighting at Seringapatam in 1799, saying that to live one day as a lion is better than to live a hundred years as a jackal.
items.e: He is remembered as a symbol of courage and freedom.

items.q3: د ملکې ویکتوریا د اعلامیې مهمې ځانګړتیاوې کومې دي؟
items.a: It ended the rule of the East India Company and put India under the Crown; the British promised not to take more land from the Indian states and to respect the rights and dignity of the Indian rulers; the subjects were promised freedom of religion and no interference in their beliefs; all were to be equal before the law and to get government jobs on merit without regard to race or religion; those who took part in the revolt were pardoned except murderers.
items.e: Proclamation of 1 November 1858.

items.q: Write a note on Lord Macaulay's Minute (1836-37).
items.q2: لارڈ میکالے کی یادداشت (1836-37) پر نوٹ لکھیں۔
items.q3: د لارډ مکاولي د یادښت (۱۸۳۶-۳۷) په اړه یادښت ولیکئ.
items.a: Lord Macaulay, law member of the Governor-General's council, wrote his Minute on education in 1835 (the book gives 1836-37). He said that European knowledge was better than Eastern learning, that English should be the medium of higher education, and that the government should create a class of Indians 'Indian in blood and colour but English in taste, opinions, morals and intellect'. The government accepted it, English became the language of education and official work, and the Persian and Arabic schools declined.
items.e: English replaced Persian as the official language.

items.q2: انگریزوں کے اقتدار میں آنے کے بعد سماجی تبدیلی کے لیے کون سے اقدامات کیے گئے؟

items.e: Social reforms under British rule.

items.q: Explain the objectives of Faraizi movement launched by Haji Shariat-ullah?
items.q2: حاجی شریعت اللہ کی شروع کی گئی تحریکِ فرائضی کے مقاصد بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د حاجي شریعت الله لخوا پیل شوي فرایضي خوځښت موخې تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Haji Shariat Ullah started the Faraizi movement in Bengal to make Muslims follow the faraiz (the obligatory duties of Islam such as prayer, fasting, zakat and Hajj), to give up un-Islamic and Hindu customs and superstitions, and to save the poor peasants from the cruelty of the Hindu landlords (zamindars).
items.e: Faraizi means those who follow the faraiz.

items.q: What was the key aim of Brahmo Samajh?
items.q2: برہمو سماج کا بنیادی مقصد کیا تھا؟
items.q3: د برهمو سماج اصلي موخه څه وه؟
items.a: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 to reform Hindu society: to worship one God and give up idol worship, to end evils such as sati, child marriage and caste differences, and to promote modern education.
items.e: A Hindu reform movement.

items.q: Why do you think the Muslims were subjected to harsh treatment by the British after the War of Independence 1857?
items.q2: آپ کے خیال میں 1857 کی جنگِ آزادی کے بعد مسلمانوں کے ساتھ انگریزوں نے سخت سلوک کیوں کیا؟
items.q3: ستاسو په فکر د ۱۸۵۷ د خپلواکۍ جګړې وروسته انګرېزانو له مسلمانانو سره ولې سخت چلند وکړ؟
items.a: The British held the Muslims mainly responsible for the war of 1857 because the revolt was fought in the name of the last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, and the Muslims had been the rulers of India before them. So they punished them: many were executed or exiled, their property was taken, and they were removed from government jobs; the British feared they would revolt again.
items.e: The Muslims were blamed as the former rulers.

items.q: What were the reasons for the formation of the Aligarh Movement?
items.q2: تحریکِ علی گڑھ کے قیام کے اسباب کیا تھے؟
items.q3: د علیګړه خوځښت د جوړېدو لاملونه کوم وو؟
items.a: After 1857 the Muslims were poor, backward and hated by the British, had lost their jobs and refused to learn English and modern science, while the Hindus advanced quickly. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan started the Aligarh Movement to remove the misunderstandings between the British and the Muslims, to spread modern education among the Muslims and to restore their position in society.
items.e: Muslim backwardness after 1857.

items.q: Who was Syed Ameer Ali? Why were his contributions important?
items.q2: سید امیر علی کون تھے؟ ان کی خدمات اہم کیوں تھیں؟
items.q3: سید امیر علي څوک و؟ د هغه خدمتونه ولې مهم وو؟
items.a: Syed Ameer Ali (1849 to 1928) was a Muslim scholar, writer and judge from Bengal. He founded the Central National Muhammadan Association (1877) in Calcutta to protect Muslim rights and wrote 'The Spirit of Islam', which defended Islam against Western criticism; he later helped the Muslim League in London. His contributions were important because they gave the Muslims political awareness and defended their religion and rights.
items.e: A leader and writer of the Muslim revival.

items.q: Explain the contributions of Sheikh Ahmad Sarhindi for the revival of Islamic teachings. Give evidences to support your explanation.
items.q2: اسلامی تعلیمات کے احیا کے لیے شیخ احمد سرہندی کی خدمات بیان کریں۔ اپنی وضاحت کی تائید میں شواہد دیں۔
items.q3: د اسلامي زده‌کړو د بیا ژوندي کولو لپاره د شیخ احمد سرهندي ونډې تشریح کړئ. خپلې تشریح ملاتړ لپاره شواهد ورکړئ.
items.a: Sheikh Ahmad Sarhindi (Mujaddid Alf Thani, 1564 to 1624) opposed Emperor Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi and the un-Islamic customs at the court, and called for the strict following of the Quran and Sunnah. He cleaned Sufism of innovations, explained that Muslims and Hindus are different nations, and wrote letters (Maktubat) to nobles and the emperor Jahangir to bring them back to Islam; as evidence, Jahangir ended Akbar's policy and the nobles returned to Islamic teachings.
items.e: He revived Islamic teachings in India.

items.q: Describe the Faraizi Movement and its impact.
items.q2: تحریکِ فرائضی اور اس کے اثرات بیان کریں۔
items.q3: فرایضي خوځښت او د هغه اغېزې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Haji Shariat Ullah started it in Bengal in the early 19th century to bring the Muslims back to the faraiz of Islam and away from Hindu customs. After him his son Dudu Miyan (Muhammad Mohsin) turned it into a movement of the peasants against the oppression of the zamindars and organised them. Impact: the Muslims of Bengal became more religious and united, the poor peasants got courage against their landlords and the British, and it prepared the way for later movements.
items.e: Founded by Haji Shariat Ullah.

items.q: Write a detailed note on Syed Ahmed Bareli's vision of Jihad.
items.q2: سید احمد بریلی کے تصورِ جہاد پر تفصیلی نوٹ لکھیں۔
items.q3: د سید احمد بریلي د جهاد د لید په اړه مفصل یادښت ولیکئ.
items.a: Syed Ahmad Barelvi (1786 to 1831) wanted to free the Muslims from the Sikhs and the British and establish an Islamic state based on the Quran and Sunnah. He organised his followers (Mujahideen), moved to the north-west frontier and declared jihad against the Sikh ruler Ranjit Singh, took Peshawar for a short time, and fought many battles. Together with Shah Ismail he was martyred at Balakot in 1831. His movement raised the spirit of jihad and was a base for later resistance to the British.
items.e: The Jihad Movement.

items.q: Explain the aims of Arya Samajh and also shed light on the influence it created under the banner of Hindu revivalist movement.
items.q2: آریہ سماج کے مقاصد بیان کریں اور ہندو احیائی تحریک کے پرچم تلے اس کے پیدا کردہ اثر پر بھی روشنی ڈالیں۔
items.q3: د آریه سماج موخې تشریح کړئ او همداراز د هندو احیايي خوځښت تر بیرغ لاندې د هغه رامنځته شوي اغېز ته رڼا واچوئ.
items.a: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875. Its aims were to return to the Vedas, to give up idol worship and later customs, to spread Hindi and Hindu culture, and to bring back converts to Hinduism (the Shuddhi movement). As a Hindu revivalist movement it made Hindus proud of their past and politically active but, because it attacked Islam and Christianity and converted Muslims back, it increased the distance and ill feeling between Hindus and Muslims.
items.e: Hindu revival.

items.q: Analyze the impacts of the educational efforts of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan on the uplift of Muslim society.
items.q2: مسلم معاشرے کی ترقی پر سر سید احمد خان کی تعلیمی کوششوں کے اثرات کا تجزیہ کریں۔
items.q3: د مسلمانې ټولنې په پورته کولو د سر سید احمدخان د زده‌کړیزو هڅو اغېزې تحلیل کړئ.
items.a: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society (1864) to translate English books, and the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh (1875), which later became Aligarh Muslim University, and started the Muhammadan Educational Conference. Impact: the Muslims accepted modern education and learned English and science, got jobs in the government, regained confidence and political awareness, and produced the educated leaders of the Pakistan Movement.
items.e: He uplifted the Muslim society through education.

items.q3: د لومړۍ نړیوالې جګړې سمدستی لامل څه و؟
items.a: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914 by a Serbian nationalist.
items.e: Austria then declared war on Serbia and the allies joined.

items.q: Why did the League of Nations fail in reaching its objectives?
items.q2: لیگ آف نیشنز اپنے مقاصد حاصل کرنے میں ناکام کیوں ہوئی؟
items.q3: د ملتونو ټولنه د خپلو موخو په ترلاسه کولو کې ولې ناکامه شوه؟
items.a: It had no army of its own to stop an aggressor; the USA never joined it and powerful members like Germany, Japan and Italy left it; decisions needed all members to agree; the big powers (Britain and France) thought of their own interests; and it could not stop Japan in Manchuria, Italy in Abyssinia or Hitler's aggression.
items.e: It failed to prevent the Second World War.

items.q: Who was Hitler? What did he promise to his nation?
items.q2: ہٹلر کون تھا؟ اس نے اپنی قوم سے کیا وعدہ کیا؟
items.q3: هټلر څوک و؟ هغه خپل ملت ته څه ژمنه وکړه؟
items.a: Adolf Hitler was the leader of the Nazi Party and the dictator (Chancellor and Fuhrer) of Germany from 1933. He promised the Germans to cancel the unfair Treaty of Versailles, to make Germany strong and proud again, to give them jobs and food after the Great Depression and to give them more land.
items.e: He started the Second World War.

items.q: Which two Japanese cities were destroyed by atomic bombs?
items.q2: کون سے دو جاپانی شہر ایٹم بموں سے تباہ ہوئے؟
items.q3: کوم دوه جاپاني ښارونه په اټومي بمونو ویجاړ شول؟
items.a: Hiroshima (6 August 1945) and Nagasaki (9 August 1945).
items.e: The USA dropped the bombs and Japan surrendered.

items.q3: د دویمې نړیوالې جګړې په پایله کې کومو هېوادونو ډېرې مرینې ولیدې؟
items.a: The Soviet Union suffered the most deaths (over 20 million), followed by China, Germany, Poland and Japan.
items.e: About 50 to 60 million people died in the war.

items.q: Do you think the United Nations could achieve its objectives?
items.q2: کیا آپ سمجھتے ہیں کہ اقوامِ متحدہ اپنے مقاصد حاصل کر سکی؟
items.q3: ایا تاسو فکر کوئ چې ملګري ملتونه خپلې موخې ترلاسه کړای شوې؟
items.a: Partly. The UN has prevented a third world war, ended many conflicts through peacekeeping, and helped with health, education, refugees and human rights. But its decisions can be blocked by the veto of the five permanent members, and problems such as Kashmir and Palestine are still unsolved. (Sample answer: your opinion with reasons is also accepted.)
items.e: Opinion question.

items.q: What do you think was the worst effect of the Cold War?
items.q2: آپ کے خیال میں سرد جنگ کا بدترین اثر کیا تھا؟
items.q3: ستاسو په فکر د سړې جګړې تر ټولو بده اغېزه څه وه؟
items.a: The arms race and the fear of nuclear war: the world was divided into two blocs, countries spent huge sums on weapons, and the rivalry caused wars in Korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan and left many countries poor and unstable. (Sample answer: your opinion with reasons is also accepted.)
items.e: Opinion question.

items.q: What are the objectives of the United Nations?
items.q2: اقوامِ متحدہ کے مقاصد کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: د ملګرو ملتونو موخې کومې دي؟
items.a: To maintain international peace and security; to develop friendly relations among nations; to bring nations together to solve economic, social, cultural and humanitarian problems; to promote respect for human rights and freedoms; and to be a centre for harmonising the actions of nations.
items.e: From the UN Charter (1945).

items.q: What do we need to do to make this world a peaceful place?
items.q2: اس دنیا کو پُرامن جگہ بنانے کے لیے ہمیں کیا کرنا چاہیے؟
items.q3: دا نړۍ د سولې ځای کولو لپاره موږ باید څه وکړو؟
items.a: Respect all religions, cultures and people, solve disputes through talks and the United Nations and not by war, reduce weapons, share resources fairly, give everyone justice and equal rights, and teach tolerance and love to children. (Sample answer: other sensible ideas are accepted.)
items.e: Opinion question.

items.q: What were the main causes of the World War I?
items.q2: پہلی جنگِ عظیم کے بنیادی اسباب کیا تھے؟
items.q3: د لومړۍ نړیوالې جګړې اصلي لاملونه کوم وو؟
items.a: Militarism (the arms race), the alliance system (the Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy against the Triple Entente of Britain, France and Russia), imperialism (competition for colonies and trade), and extreme nationalism, especially in the Balkans. The immediate cause was the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo in 1914.
items.e: Main and immediate causes.

items.q: Critically analyse the causes behind the World War II keeping in mind the destruction caused by this war.
items.q2: اس جنگ سے ہونے والی تباہی کو مدنظر رکھتے ہوئے دوسری جنگِ عظیم کے پیچھے اسباب کا تنقیدی تجزیہ کریں۔
items.q3: د دې جګړې لخوا رامنځته شوې ویجاړۍ په پام کې نیولو سره د دویمې نړیوالې جګړې شا ته لاملونه په انتقادي ډول تحلیل کړئ.
items.a: Causes: the harsh Treaty of Versailles that left Germany angry; the Great Depression of 1929 that caused poverty and helped dictators like Hitler, Mussolini and the Japanese militarists to come to power; the failure of the League of Nations; aggression by Japan (Manchuria), Italy (Abyssinia) and Germany (Austria, Czechoslovakia); and Britain and France's policy of appeasement. The war began when Germany attacked Poland on 1 September 1939. The destruction was enormous: about 50 to 60 million people died, cities were ruined, millions suffered in the Holocaust, and the atomic bombs destroyed Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
items.e: Causes of the Second World War.

items.q: What are the causes of the formation of the United Nations? Enlist its main organs.
items.q2: اقوامِ متحدہ کے قیام کے اسباب کیا ہیں؟ اس کے اہم اداروں کی فہرست بنائیں۔
items.q3: د ملګرو ملتونو د جوړېدو لاملونه کوم دي؟ اصلي ارکان یې لیست کړئ.
items.a: Causes: the League of Nations had failed to stop the Second World War, and the world wanted a stronger organisation to prevent another such destruction and to protect peace and human rights. The UN was founded on 24 October 1945 after the San Francisco Conference. Its main organs are the General Assembly, the Security Council, the Economic and Social Council, the Trusteeship Council, the International Court of Justice and the Secretariat.
items.e: Six main organs.

items.q: Write a note on the Cold War.
items.q2: سرد جنگ پر نوٹ لکھیں۔
items.q3: د سړې جګړې په اړه یادښت ولیکئ.
items.a: The Cold War (1945 to 1991) was a period of tension, rivalry and propaganda between the two superpowers, the capitalist USA with its allies (NATO) and the communist Soviet Union with its allies (Warsaw Pact), without a direct war between them. It showed in an arms and nuclear race, a space race and wars fought in other countries (Korea, Vietnam, Afghanistan), and in crises like the Cuban missile crisis (1962). It ended when the Soviet Union broke up in 1991.
items.e: USA against USSR.

items.q: Enlist primary objectives of All India Muslim League.
items.q2: آل انڈیا مسلم لیگ کے بنیادی مقاصد کی فہرست بنائیں۔
items.q3: د آل انډیا مسلم لیګ اصلي موخې ولیکئ.
items.a: The Muslim League was founded at Dhaka in 1906 with these objectives: to create among the Muslims of India loyalty to the British government and remove misunderstandings; to protect and advance the political rights and interests of the Muslims and put their needs before the government; and to prevent ill feeling between the Muslims and other communities.
items.e: Aims of the Muslim League (1906).

items.q: What was the significance of the Khilafat Movement in the creation of Pakistan?
items.q2: قیامِ پاکستان میں تحریکِ خلافت کی کیا اہمیت تھی؟
items.q3: د پاکستان په رامنځته کېدو کې د خلافت خوځښت اهمیت څه و؟
items.a: The Khilafat Movement (1919 to 1924) united the Muslims of India for the first time in a mass political movement, awakened their political awareness and taught them organisation and sacrifice. When the Hindu-Muslim unity ended with the failure of the movement and the riots that followed, the Muslims saw that they must look after their own interests, which strengthened the idea of a separate Muslim homeland.
items.e: It strengthened Muslim identity.

items.q: Do you think Nehru Report paved the way for the creation of Pakistan? Give reasons.
items.q2: کیا آپ سمجھتے ہیں کہ نہرو رپورٹ نے قیامِ پاکستان کی راہ ہموار کی؟ وجوہات دیں۔
items.q3: ایا تاسو فکر کوئ چې د نهرو راپور د پاکستان د رامنځته کېدو لار هواره کړه؟ دلایل ورکړئ.
items.a: Yes. The Nehru Report (1928) rejected separate electorates and reserved seats for Muslims and a federal system with strong provinces, and the Congress refused Jinnah's amendments. The Muslims felt that the Hindu majority would not protect their rights, so Jinnah answered with his Fourteen Points (1929) and the Muslims moved towards the demand for a separate homeland.
items.e: Reasons: the Muslims lost trust in the Congress.

items.q: How did the Congress Ministries come to an end in 1939?
items.q2: 1939 میں کانگریسی وزارتوں کا خاتمہ کیسے ہوا؟
items.q3: په ۱۹۳۹ کې د کانګرس وزارتونه څنګه پای ته ورسېدل؟
items.a: When the Second World War began in September 1939 the Viceroy, Lord Linlithgow, declared India at war without asking the Indian leaders. The Congress protested and its ministries resigned in all the provinces in October-November 1939. The Muslims, relieved, celebrated 22 December 1939 as the Day of Deliverance (Yaum-e-Nijat) on the call of Quaid-e-Azam.
items.e: Resignation of the Congress ministries.

items.q: Why is the Pakistan Resolution an important landmark in Pakistan Movement?
items.q2: قراردادِ پاکستان تحریکِ پاکستان میں ایک اہم سنگِ میل کیوں ہے؟
items.q3: د پاکستان قرارداد د پاکستان په خوځښت کې مهم کېږدی ولې دی؟
items.a: It was the first clear demand for separate independent states for the Muslims of India in the areas where they were in a majority, passed on 23 March 1940 at Lahore. It gave the Muslims a goal and a name for their struggle, and the Pakistan Movement became a mass movement that achieved Pakistan within seven years.
items.e: The Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution, 1940.

items.q: Write a note on the Congress Ministries after 1937 elections.
items.q2: 1937 کے انتخابات کے بعد کانگریسی وزارتوں پر نوٹ لکھیں۔
items.q3: د ۱۹۳۷ ټاکنو وروسته د کانګرس وزارتونو په اړه یادښت ولیکئ.
items.a: In the elections of 1937 the Congress won a clear majority in five provinces and formed ministries in seven (later eight) of the eleven provinces, while the Muslim League did poorly. The Congress ministries treated the Muslims unfairly: Bande Mataram was made compulsory in schools, the Wardha and Vidya Mandir schemes tried to hide the Muslim culture, Urdu was pushed down in favour of Hindi, cow slaughter was banned and Muslims were harassed. The Muslim League collected such complaints in reports (the Pirpur Report). The ministries resigned in 1939.
items.e: Rule of the Congress, 1937 to 1939.

items.q: Describe the Lahore Resolution and its significance.
items.q2: قراردادِ لاہور اور اس کی اہمیت بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د لاهور قرارداد او د هغه اهمیت بیان کړئ.
items.a: The Lahore Resolution was moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and passed on 23 March 1940 at the annual session of the Muslim League at Minto Park, Lahore, under Quaid-e-Azam. It said that the areas where the Muslims are in a majority, such as the north-western and eastern zones of India, should be grouped to form independent states, with their units autonomous and sovereign, and that safeguards must be given to the minorities. Its significance: it officially declared the aim of a separate Muslim homeland (the Hindu press called it the Pakistan Resolution) and turned the freedom movement into the Pakistan Movement.
items.e: Lahore Resolution, 1940.

items.q: How did the Muslim League obtain success in the 1945-46 elections? Why were these elections important for the fate of the country?
items.q2: مسلم لیگ نے 1945-46 کے انتخابات میں کامیابی کیسے حاصل کی؟ یہ انتخابات ملک کی تقدیر کے لیے کیوں اہم تھے؟
items.q3: مسلم لیګ په ۱۹۴۵-۴۶ ټاکنو کې بریا څنګه ترلاسه کړه؟ دا ټاکنې د هېواد د برخلیک لپاره ولې مهمې وې؟
items.a: The Muslim League won all 30 Muslim seats in the Central Assembly and about 90 percent of the Muslim seats in the provinces. It succeeded because of the leadership of Quaid-e-Azam, the clear demand for Pakistan, the unity of the Muslims in the League's campaign, the work of the students and women, and the Congress rule that had made the Muslims distrust it. These elections were important because they proved that the Muslim League was the only representative of the Muslims, so the British and the Congress had to accept the demand for Pakistan.
items.e: Elections of 1945-46.

items.q: Analyze the factors that led to landmark victory of All India Muslim League in 1945-46 elections.
items.q2: 1945-46 کے انتخابات میں آل انڈیا مسلم لیگ کی تاریخی فتح کا باعث بننے والے عوامل کا تجزیہ کریں۔

items.a: Factors: the strong and honest leadership of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah; the Pakistan slogan and the Lahore Resolution that united the Muslims; the unfair rule of the Congress ministries (1937 to 1939); the organisation of the League in every province and the help of students, women, the ulema and the press; and the fear of the Muslims that they would be ruled by the Hindu majority. As a result the League won all the Muslim seats of the Central Assembly and about 90 percent of the Muslim seats of the provinces.
items.e: Why the Muslims voted for the League.

items.q: Evaluate the most challenging problem Pakistan had to face after Independence.

items.a: The most challenging problem was the settlement of the refugees: about eight million Muslims came from India with nothing, and had to be given food, shelter and work in a new country with few resources. At the same time Pakistan had no capital buildings or offices, little money because India held back its share of the assets, and the Kashmir and canal water disputes. items.q: What was the constitutional arrangement in Pakistan before 1956 constitution?
items.q2: 1956 کے آئین سے پہلے پاکستان میں آئینی انتظام کیا تھا؟
items.q3: د ۱۹۵۶ د اساسي قانون مخکې په پاکستان کې اساسي ترتیب څه و؟
items.a: Until 1956 Pakistan was governed under the Government of India Act 1935 with changes, as an interim constitution by the Indian Independence Act 1947. The Governor-General was the head of state, and the Constituent Assembly worked as both the law-making body and the body writing the constitution. The Objectives Resolution (1949) gave the guiding principles for the future constitution.
items.e: Interim constitution.

items.q: Why has Objectives Resolution become a compulsory part of all the constitutions of Pakistan?
items.q2: قراردادِ مقاصد پاکستان کے تمام آئینوں کا لازمی حصہ کیوں بن گئی ہے؟
items.q3: د مقاصدو قرارداد د پاکستان د ټولو اساسي قوانینو لازمي برخه ولې شوې؟
items.a: The Objectives Resolution (1949) states the basic principles on which Pakistan was founded: the sovereignty belongs to Allah, the people use their power within the limits set by Him, democracy, freedom, equality and tolerance according to Islam, the rights of the minorities and an independent judiciary. Because it expresses the ideology of Pakistan it was made the preamble of the constitutions of 1956, 1962 and 1973, and a binding part of the 1973 constitution (Article 2A).
items.e: The guiding principles.

items.q: Compare the constitution of 1962 with the constitution of 1973.
items.q2: آئینِ 1962 کا آئینِ 1973 سے موازنہ کریں۔
items.q3: د ۱۹۶۲ اساسي قانون له ۱۹۷۳ اساسي قانون سره پرتله کړئ.
items.a: The constitution of 1962 gave a presidential system in which the President had very wide powers and was elected by the Basic Democrats (indirectly), with a one-house National Assembly and weak fundamental rights and provinces. The constitution of 1973 gives a parliamentary federal system in which the Prime Minister is the real head of government and the President is head of state, with a two-house Parliament (the National Assembly and the Senate), direct elections, fundamental rights, independent judiciary and provincial rights; it is the permanent constitution.
items.e: 1962 presidential, 1973 parliamentary.

In the 1965 war it attacked the Indian radar station at Dwarka, and in 1971 it fought bravely, with the submarine Hangor sinking the Indian frigate Khukri.

items.q: Briefly describe the nature of Kashmir conflict between India and Pakistan. How can it be resolved?
items.q2: بھارت اور پاکستان کے درمیان تنازعہ کشمیر کی نوعیت مختصراً بیان کریں۔ اسے کیسے حل کیا جا سکتا ہے؟
items.q3: د هند او پاکستان ترمنځ د کشمیر د شخړې ماهیت په لنډه توګه بیان کړئ. دا څنګه حل کېدای شي؟
items.a: Kashmir was a princely state with a Muslim majority. In 1947 its Hindu Maharaja Hari Singh joined India against the wish of the people, the Kashmiris rose up and the first war followed (1947-48). The matter went to the UN Security Council, which passed resolutions in 1948-49 giving the Kashmiris the right to decide their future through a plebiscite, but India has never held it; a ceasefire line (now the Line of Control) divides the state, and the 1965 war was fought over it. It can be resolved by talks and by giving the Kashmiris their right of self-determination under the UN resolutions.
items.e: A dispute between Pakistan and India.

Events: India attacked East and West Pakistan on 3 December 1971; the Pakistani army in the east was surrounded, and on 16 December 1971 it surrendered at Dhaka, and East Pakistan became Bangladesh.

items.a: Poverty and the shortage of schools, teachers and facilities, especially in villages, together with the fast growth of population and little money spent on education, so that more than 22 million children are out of school; many poor families send their children to work instead. items.q: Discuss the role of the Executive in the country.
items.q2: ملک میں انتظامیہ کے کردار پر بحث کریں۔
items.q3: په هېواد کې د اجرایې د رول په اړه بحث وکړئ.
items.a: The Executive is the branch of government that carries out the laws made by the Parliament. It consists of the President, the Prime Minister and the Cabinet with the ministries and the civil servants. It runs the administration, makes and carries out the policies, collects taxes, looks after defence and foreign affairs, and keeps law and order.
items.e: The three organs: legislature, executive, judiciary.

items.q: Why should judiciary be separate from executive?
items.q2: عدلیہ کو انتظامیہ سے الگ کیوں ہونا چاہیے؟
items.q3: قضا ولې باید له اجرایې څخه بېله وي؟
items.a: So that judges can decide cases freely and fairly without pressure or fear from the government, protect the rights of the citizens even against the government, and check that the executive does not misuse its power. If the executive controlled the courts, there would be no real justice.
items.e: Separation of powers.

items.a: Build and repair playgrounds, stadiums and sports complexes in every town; make sports a regular part of school and college life; give good coaching, scholarships and jobs to players; choose teams on merit without favour; give them sponsors and money and send them to international tournaments; encourage girls and women; and provide proper food and training.
