items.a: Agriculture gives 18.5 percent of the GDP and 38.5 percent of the jobs of Pakistan, feeds the people and earns foreign exchange. Since 1947 production has increased manifold: wheat from 3.30 to 25.49 million tonnes, cotton from 0.188 to 11.93 million bales, rice from 6.92 to 7.44 million tonnes, citrus from 0.08 to 2.39 million tonnes and sugarcane from 5.52 to 81.10 million tonnes by 2018.

items.q: Briefly describe development of Pakistan in the field of Industry.

items.q3: د صنعت په برخه کې د پاکستان پرمختګ په لنډه توګه بیان کړئ.
items.a: At independence Pakistan had only 34 industries out of 921 in the subcontinent (about four percent). Since then it has built the textile industry (the largest), sugar, cement, fertilizer, iron and steel (Pakistan Steel Mills), the Heavy Mechanical Complex and Port Qasim, and is now the third largest exporter of cotton textile in the world.

items.a: The Parliament of Pakistan is the law-making body and has two houses: the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house); the President is also a part of it. The National Assembly has 342 members (272 elected by direct vote, 60 seats for women and 10 for religious minorities) elected for five years. The Senate has equal representation of all the federating units (100 members in the book, elected for six years) so that all provinces have an equal voice.

items.q: Write a note on Judiciary of Pakistan.
items.q2: پاکستان کی عدلیہ پر نوٹ لکھیں۔
items.q3: د پاکستان د قضا په اړه یادښت ولیکئ.
items.a: The judiciary is the organ of the state that interprets the laws and gives justice. At the top is the Supreme Court of Pakistan at Islamabad, below it are the High Courts of the provinces and Islamabad, the Federal Shariat Court, and the district and session courts and the civil courts. The judges are appointed by the President on the advice of the Judicial Commission, are independent, protect the constitution and the fundamental rights, and decide disputes.
items.e: Courts of Pakistan.

items.q: Describe the role of Pakistan in the United Nations Organization.
items.q2: اقوامِ متحدہ میں پاکستان کے کردار کو بیان کریں۔
items.q3: په ملګرو ملتونو کې د پاکستان رول بیان کړئ.
items.a: Pakistan has been a member of the UN since 30 September 1947. It is one of the largest contributors of troops to the UN peacekeeping missions in many countries, has been elected several times to the Security Council, supports the right of self-determination of the Kashmiris and Palestinians, and works for disarmament, human rights and development.
items.e: Pakistan and the UN.

items.q: Compare Pakistan's role in SAARC and OIC.
items.q2: سارک اور او آئی سی میں پاکستان کے کردار کا موازنہ کریں۔
items.q3: په SAARC او OIC کې د پاکستان رول پرتله کړئ.
items.a: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, founded in 1985) is a regional organisation of eight countries for cooperation and friendship in South Asia; Pakistan has played an important role, hosting the 4th summit (1988) and the 12th summit (2004) at Islamabad and being the second largest contributor to its budget. The OIC (Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, founded in 1969) is the organisation of Muslim countries for unity and the solving of their problems; Pakistan, a founding supporter, hosted the Lahore summit in 1974 and always speaks for Kashmir and Palestine. SAARC is regional, the OIC is based on religion and spread over many continents.
items.e: Pakistan's role in both.
